Rerun 2026-10-15 via app._align_core SIFT_RANSAC path (cv2.setRNGSeed(0)), audited 2048x2048 windows (fore col_off=361 row_off=93328; nadir col_off=416 row_off=101611) at native TMC-2 scale. Original table value 27.351923 px reproduced at 28.031705 px (delta 0.68 px). Circularity guard PASS. NOT a unit error: pixel_scale_m=4.47 was used in both runs; the 28 px are native window pixels = ~125 m. Root cause: the 13 SIFT inliers collapsed to a thin horizontal strip (ref y in [944,1096] of 2048) while GT landmarks span y in [218,1965]; the global partial-affine extrapolates badly outside the strip (residual grows with |y-1100|, up to 54 px). Best-fit homography on the GT points themselves achieves 3.20 px RMSE, so the landmarks are internally consistent and a far better global 2D model exists -- the gap is the strip-constrained 4-DoF fit, plus real fore/nadir viewing-geometry difference (fit scale 0.90 suggests foreshortening). Pipeline inlier RMSE 1.77 px understates the frame-wide human-landmark RMSE by ~16x. Quadrant entropy (1.95, 4/4) did not catch the strip collapse because the strip straddles the y=1024 quadrant boundary.
